title: From the Editor — The Useful Lie
settingText: Bellweather in light rain: weathered family houses, wet dust, covered porch tables, dim warm windows, mourning cloth and ordinary domestic objects. No funeral body, no identity reveal, no identifiable cast close-ups.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They found the people behind the trick.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: That should have made everything simpler.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Raina James had a theory. Samuel Hayes helped test it. Real names, real grievances, carefully placed expectations. Put Brandon in front of the right wound and see what he knows.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Some of the road can now be explained.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: There is one more story Samuel set in motion before the truth caught up with him.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: So is a family burying one of its own.

title: One More Setup
summary: Raina admits that one of Samuel's planted identities is still waiting ahead at Bellweather: Nathan Bell, the estranged son of a woman whose wake has already begun. Brandon could avoid the place, but chooses to go because someone has already put his face inside a grieving family's business.

panelPlan.text: At a roadside camp, Raina lays Samuel's old route notes on a blanket. One remaining name is circled: NATHAN BELL — BELLWEATHER.
Samuel explains that he spoke to one cousin before the relay confrontation. He has not returned since.
Brandon folds the note once and hands it back. Eva expects him to detour. Instead he asks how far Bellweather is.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: I was there before the relay. I told a cousin Nathan Bell might come home.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Anyone there likely to pull a gun?

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: No guns that I know of. Family. Grief. Old arguments.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: You want to walk into it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: They've been waiting for a man who looks like me. I'd rather clear that up.

title: The Wake
summary: Bellweather is in the middle of Mary Bell's mother's three-day wake, when unresolved promises to the dead are spoken aloud. Mary and Owen see Brandon and immediately pull him into the absent Nathan's place in the family.

panelPlan.text: Bellweather is a clustered family settlement around a shaded courtyard. Food, chairs and sleeping children make the wake feel lived-in rather than ceremonial spectacle.
Mary Bell sees Brandon at the gate and stops with a serving bowl in both hands. Owen rises more slowly, angry before he is convinced.
Brandon removes his hat out of ordinary respect for the wake and tells them his name before either sibling can finish welcoming Nathan home.

title: What the Dead Promised
summary: The Bell siblings' real conflict surfaces. Their mother promised a tenant family permanent use of two houses, but Owen claims only Nathan heard the promise and therefore only Nathan can settle it. Brandon refuses to become the missing witness.

panelPlan.text: At the long wake table, Owen argues that kindness would be telling Mary what their mother promised, while another relative points out that there is no written record. The rest of the family listens closely.
Owen pushes a family token toward Brandon and asks Nathan to say what their mother told him. Brandon does not touch it.
Eva watches how easily one sentence from Brandon could end the argument; Jessie watches Brandon instead of the table.

dialogueInline.speaker: Owen Bell
dialogueInline.text: Kind would be telling Mary what Mom promised.

dialogueInline.speaker: Owen Bell
dialogueInline.text: You expect us to believe you forgot your own mother?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: No. I expect you to believe I'm not your brother.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mary Bell
dialogueInline.text: If you would just say she promised—

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Because someone told you I was coming.

title: The Useful Lie
summary: Eva argues privately that Brandon could pretend for five minutes and spare the family a fight. Jessie pushes back, and the disagreement becomes the first time the women clearly reveal different instincts through their theories about him.

panelPlan.text: Eva follows Brandon's reason for coming with the obvious counterargument: now that he is here, he could help. Behind the Bell house she catches Brandon and Jessie near the water jars while the wake continues inside.
Eva makes the practical case for one harmless performance. Brandon listens longer than she expects before answering.
Jessie points out that Eva is treating the end of the scene as the end of the consequence. Eva realizes Jessie is defending Brandon's position, and teases her about it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: And now that you're here, you could help.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: And when Owen asks what else his brother remembers?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: So now you need a second lie to keep the first one going.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I'm trying to stop a family from tearing itself apart over two houses.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: You want it settled before we leave. That's not the same thing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I'm still not lying for them.

title: The Detail Samuel Missed
summary: Mary mentions that the man who prepared them for Nathan also knew a private Bell family phrase Samuel insists he never heard or repeated. Raina arrives expecting to audit her own setup and instead finds evidence that the story had acquired information outside her control.

panelPlan.text: Mary interrupts the argument over a useful lie with a problem Samuel might actually answer. Raina and Samuel have reached Bellweather late in the wake. Mary is furious when she recognizes Samuel's coat.
She repeats the phrase Samuel used: 'the blue room stays open.' Samuel goes still, opens his route notebook and checks the page; the phrase is absent.
Raina checks Samuel's old page anyway. Brandon does not crowd the discovery; he is helping carry chairs back under the awning.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mary Bell
dialogueInline.text: Then maybe Samuel can explain this.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mary Bell
dialogueInline.text: You remember me saying, 'the blue room stays open.'

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: I believe you. Someone else gave you that detail.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Could she have told you earlier and forgotten?

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: She never gave me that detail.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Could someone have told her after you left?

dialogueInline.speaker: Mary Bell
dialogueInline.text: No one knew I was waiting for Nathan except family.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Start after we get the tables in. It's raining.

title: After the Wake
summary: The Bell family resolves the housing promise through living witnesses and their own willingness to honor it, not through Brandon impersonating Nathan. Brandon explains to Eva why the lie would have been worse precisely because it might have worked.

panelPlan.text: After the rain and the unexplained blue-room phrase, an elderly aunt confirms enough of the dead woman's promise that Mary and Owen can decide what they are willing to honor. The tenant family is present but not reduced to props.
Outside after the wake, Eva sits on the rig step while Brandon washes a borrowed plate. Jessie listens without pretending not to.
Raina and Samuel remain behind speaking with Mary about the unexplained phrase. The trio leaves before their investigation turns the wake back into a test.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You could've stopped Owen and Mary fighting.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I could've stopped the argument. I couldn't make it true.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Not if tomorrow depends on something I made up.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You really worry about what happens after we leave, don't you?

title: Next: BRANNOCK STAYED
settingText: A long road curling back toward the Last Drop. In the far distance, the exterior wall with its crude human mural catches the last light. The returning travelers remain tiny and unidentifiable.
